meta.title: EC2 Launch and Flask Deployment on Beanstalk

slides.title: EC2 Launch and Flask Deployment on Beanstalk
EC2 Plus Beanstalk
slides.lead: Launch an EC2 instance, then deploy a Flask app on Elastic Beanstalk, to compare self-managed and managed provisioning live

steps.text: Sign in to the AWS console and select the Mumbai region
Launch an EC2 instance with a chosen AMI, instance type and key pair
Connect to the instance and run basic verification commands
Package a small Flask application as a ZIP archive
Create an Elastic Beanstalk application and environment from the ZIP
Deploy and verify Version 1, then update to Version 2
Clean up every resource created to avoid charges

slides.label: Instance Running With Status Checks Passed

props.title: Image and Sizing Choices
props.lead: The instance launches from a machine image on a general-purpose size, with a security group allowing only the learner’s own IP for remote access
props.step: Instance Running With Status Checks Passed
props.caption: s9-ec2-vm-demo in Running state with 3/3 status checks passed

points.text: AMI Amazon Linux 2023 on a `t3.micro` instance
Security group `s9-ec2-sg` allowing SSH (port 22) from My IP only

props.title: Confirming Access
props.lead: A browser-based terminal opens on the instance through SSH from a local terminal using the private key (.pem) file, and basic Linux commands confirm access
props.caption: `whoami`, `hostname`, `uname -a` and os-release output on the instance

slides.label: Application Files In The Project Folder

props.title: Files Before Upload
props.lead: The Flask application file and dependency list are archived in a ZIP with both files at the root, not inside a folder
props.step: Application Files In The Project Folder
props.caption: `application.py` and `requirements.txt` in the `s9-paas-demo` folder

props.title: First Deployment Live
props.lead:
The ZIP is uploaded to a new Elastic Beanstalk environment on the Python platform, which provisions and manages the servers for us, unlike the EC2 VM we managed ourselves
Behind the scenes, Beanstalk creates the EC2 instances, an auto scaling group and a launch template
props.caption: S9-paas-demo-env with Health Ok

slides.label: Version 2 Served At The Same URL

props.title: Redeploy and Confirm
props.lead: The code is updated, re-zipped as Version 2 and deployed to the same environment, with no new server created
props.step: Version 2 Served At The Same URL
props.caption: Version 2 page served at the same environment URL

steps.text: Verify that the Version 2 page loads at the same URL and the running version is the latest upload
Clean up to avoid charges: terminate the EC2 instance, the Elastic Beanstalk environment and delete the Beanstalk application
Then delete security group `s9-ec2-sg`, empty and delete the Beanstalk S3 bucket (`elasticbeanstalk-ap-south-1-…`), and check for leftover EBS volumes and Elastic IP addresses
